revision_instructions: Item 11a: The claim 'ISO 20022 introduced over 900 data fields per payment message — compared to 140 characters in a legacy MT103 wire' contains specific comparative figures. Add an inline citation to a named verifiable source (e.g. SWIFT documentation, ISO 20022 organisation, BAFT, or a named fintech publication). If a verifiable source cannot be identified, rewrite to a general description without the specific numbers: e.g. 'ISO 20022 introduced a far richer structured field set than the 140-character limit of legacy MT103 messages — supporting granular party identification, remittance data, and regulatory fields that MT103 could not carry.' This removes the unverifiable specifics while preserving the substance.

Item 11b: The claim 'catch the governance failure at the point of data entry, where repair costs 10x less than fixing it downstream' contains a specific ratio with no source. This appears to be derived from the data quality literature (Redman, DAMA, or similar). Either: (1) add an inline citation to a named source (e.g. 'Thomas Redman, Harvard Business Review, 2016' or 'IBM Institute for Business Value, year'); or (2) rewrite to remove the specific ratio while preserving the principle: e.g. 'catch the governance failure at the point of data entry, where the cost of repair is a fraction of what it becomes downstream.' Do not use 'significantly' — that is vague. Use a directional description instead.
